details: Bitcoin experienced volatile trading around the $64,000 mark. This follows significant institutional activity, with spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recording $225.18 million in net outflows on July 24, which ended a seven-session inflow streak. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index currently sits at 27, indicating a sentiment of "fear" in the market. The total cryptocurrency market capitalization saw a 1.1% decline, settling at $2.28 trillion.
title: Bitcoin Fluctuates Around $64K After $225M ETF Outflow

details: The ongoing escalation of US-Iran tensions in the Middle East is significantly increasing geopolitical risk for financial markets. This instability has led to a recent surge in oil prices, with Brent and WTI crude futures jumping approximately 30% in recent weeks. The rising energy costs and conflict-related uncertainty are fueling fears of "stagflationary impulses" and higher inflation, prompting expectations for the Federal Reserve to potentially increase benchmark rates, with projections suggesting a peak near 4.23% by June of next year.
title: Iran Conflict Escalates, Fueling Stagflation Fears & Rate Hike Bets

details: The Bank Policy Institute (BPI) and other banking associations have provided feedback on the recently updated Clarity Act stablecoin bill. While generally supportive of establishing a regulatory framework for digital assets, they voiced concerns that the proposed legislation's current language could permit interest-like payments for holding stablecoins. They argue this might divert deposits from traditional banks and potentially threaten local lending and economic activity. Additionally, the BPI highlighted existing Anti-Money Laundering (AML) gaps within the bill.
title: Banking Industry Raises Concerns on Updated Stablecoin Bill

details: President Donald Trump has implemented a new round of import taxes, ranging from 10% to 12.5%, on most goods originating from nearly 60 trading partners. These partners include major economies such as the European Union, Canada, Japan, and Mexico. The new tariffs, which replace previous temporary global duties, are reportedly based on allegations of forced labor conditions within the economies investigated by the Office of the United States Trade Representative.
title: Trump Imposes New Tariffs on Key US Trading Partners

details: On July 23, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council announced its decision to maintain the three key ECB interest rates at their current levels. During the press conference, President Christine Lagarde highlighted the significant uncertainty stemming from the Middle East conflict and its resulting energy shock. She reiterated the ECB's commitment to a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach for future monetary policy decisions, noting that risks to the inflation outlook remain on the upside.
title: ECB Holds Key Interest Rates Steady Amid Inflation & War Risks
